title: Accessibility: labels, traits, Dynamic Type and VoiceOver

videos.script: Close your eyes and use your phone. {{voiceover}} That is what VoiceOver is: the screen read aloud, one element at a time. And what it says for each element is something the app decides. {{row}} A session row draws a title, a number, a unit and a tick. To the ear, that is four fragments. {{label}} So the planner gives the row one sentence, a label, and a value that says whether it is done. That sentence is plain Swift, and you test it on Linux, in English and in Portuguese. {{traits}} Then traits, which tell VoiceOver what an element is: a button, a heading. {{grouping}} Then grouping, which decides how many stops a row makes. {{type}} Then Dynamic Type, where the person picks the size of the text. {{contrast}} And contrast, which is pure arithmetic. You measure six of the planner's colours, and two of them fail. Every rule helps. None of them replaces listening.
